lines: Thomas Lipton, grocer and tea merchant, worked for some years in
America before he came home to Glasgow. There he opened his first
shop, Lipton's Market, in Stobcross Street, Glasgow, in 1871.
His shops spread across Britain, and he later bought tea estates
in Ceylon to sell tea from his own gardens.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: Your Lipton tea bag is named after a shopkeeper from Glasgow.

beats.speaker: narrator

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: He opened his first Glasgow shop in 1871, and he wanted no middlemen between him and his customers.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: So in 1890 he went to Ceylon, now Sri Lanka, and bought tea estates of his own.

items.title: From Tea Garden To Teapot: How Lipton Became An Empire

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: His packs promised tea straight from his gardens, and his name went up over the factory.

place: tea pickers on a Ceylon estate

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: But his gardens could never fill every pack. NPR found he bought from brokers too, and only a small part came from his own estates.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: The name stuck anyway. In the end, Unilever sold the tea business that held Lipton, 34 brands in all, for €4.5B.
